candidate_relations.reason: The clinical record explicitly names high-grade clear-cell SCC as one of two differential diagnoses considered and then rejected in favor of the final diagnosis. The histologic hallmarks described—multivacuolated cytoplasm, pagetoid intraepidermal spread, and lobular architecture—are characteristic of sebaceous carcinoma, not squamous cell carcinoma. Asserting SCC conflicts with the benchmark reference at the subtype level.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: High-grade clear-cell squamous cell carcinoma is a distinct histologic entity from sebaceous carcinoma; both were listed in the clinical differential but the biopsy features (multivacuolated clear cells, pagetoid spread, large irregular nests/lobules) favor sebaceous carcinoma over SCC

case_quality_flags: Sebaceous carcinoma of the glans penis is rare; the clinical record provides strong histologic discriminators (multivacuolated clear cells, pagetoid spread) that distinguish it from the differential diagnoses listed.
